182	/**
183	 * Safely resolves a file path, handling symlinks and errors gracefully.
184	 *
185	 * Error handling strategy:
186	 * - If the file doesn't exist, returns the original path (allows for file creation)
187	 * - If symlink resolution fails (broken symlink, permission denied, circular links),
188	 *   returns the original path and marks it as not a symlink
189	 * - This ensures operations can continue with the original path rather than failing
190	 *
191	 * @param fs The filesystem implementation to use
192	 * @param filePath The path to resolve
193	 * @returns Object containing the resolved path and whether it was a symlink
194	 */
195	export function safeResolvePath(
196	  fs: FsOperations,
197	  filePath: string,
198	): { resolvedPath: string; isSymlink: boolean; isCanonical: boolean } {
199	  // Block UNC paths before any filesystem access to prevent network
200	  // requests (DNS/SMB) during validation on Windows
201	  if (filePath.startsWith('//') || filePath.startsWith('\\\\')) {
202	    return { resolvedPath: filePath, isSymlink: false, isCanonical: false }
203	  }
204	
205	  try {
206	    // Check for special file types (FIFOs, sockets, devices) before calling realpathSync.
207	    // realpathSync can block on FIFOs waiting for a writer, causing hangs.
208	    // If the file doesn't exist, lstatSync throws ENOENT which the catch
209	    // below handles by returning the original path (allows file creation).
210	    const stats = fs.lstatSync(filePath)
211	    if (
212	      stats.isFIFO() ||
213	      stats.isSocket() ||
214	      stats.isCharacterDevice() ||
215	      stats.isBlockDevice()
216	    ) {
217	      return { resolvedPath: filePath, isSymlink: false, isCanonical: false }
218	    }
219	
220	    const resolvedPath = fs.realpathSync(filePath)
221	    return {
222	      resolvedPath,
223	      isSymlink: resolvedPath !== filePath,
224	      // realpathSync returned: resolvedPath is canonical (all symlinks in
225	      // all path components resolved). Callers can skip further symlink
226	      // resolution on this path.
227	      isCanonical: true,
228	    }

content.text: Confirmado: `safeResolvePath` importado de `@thyrox/storage/fsOperations.js` (línea 179) tiene la firma `(fs: FsOperations, filePath: string) => { resolvedPath, isSymlink, isCanonical }` — resuelve symlinks. El binding que `setSafeResolvePathFn` espera es otra función, completamente distinta, definida en `@thyrox/config/plugin/_deps.ts:246` como `(base: string, rel: string) => string | null` — previene escape de ruta. Son dos funciones con el mismo nombre y propósito distinto; la línea 504 llama a la equivocada. El mismo defecto exacto existe verbatim en la fuente (`.../packages/app-host/src/runtime/installPluginBindings.ts:455` y `.../packages/storage/src/fsOperations.ts:138-141`), así que no es estrictez introducida por el porte — es un bug latente del original. Corregirlo de verdad exige escribir la lógica de validación de escape de ruta desde cero (no hay ninguna implementación existente de esa firma para reutilizar; medí que el binding no tiene ningún consumidor en el árbol), lo cual excede "un tipo, una guarda que el flujo ya garantiza, un valor por defecto que el código ya asume" — sería inventar comportamiento nuevo, no ajustar tipos.
